requirements.requirement: Provision the local accounts designer, reviewer, and visitor with access-group membership that permits designer/reviewer collaboration while excluding visitor.
requirements.summary: All three local accounts exist. Designer and reviewer are members of projecthandoff, while visitor is not; the identities persisted across restart.

requirements.requirement: Provide persistent inherited access under /srv/legacy2/inherited-directory-acls/projects so new designer-created directories and documents remain designer-owned, are readable and writable by reviewer, and are inaccessible to visitor, without a periodic permission-repair job.
requirements.summary: Default POSIX ACLs are present. Tests using umask 077 directly show designer ownership, inherited reviewer read/write access, and visitor traversal/read/write denial. The behavior was repeated successfully after a restart, and the final inspection found no custom cron or systemd permission-fixing job.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the existing project contents while applying the access handoff.
requirements.summary: The pre-existing brief.txt retained its 50-byte size and baseline SHA-256 throughout configuration, functional testing, restart, cleanup, and final inspection. Temporary proof content was removed.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0. ACL tooling was installed from the configured RHEL 10 BaseOS repository, and post-execution package health remained successful.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct functional and final-state evidence. Inherited ACL behavior, ownership, reviewer access, visitor denial, content preservation, platform retention, and restart persistence were coherently demonstrated. The sole hygiene defect is a retained reboot log in /tmp.
limitations: Lifecycle inventories are bounded rather than exhaustive; within their captured scope, no operational defect was found beyond the retained reboot log.
Requirement R3 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear roles: installing required ACL tooling, provisioning identities, applying ACLs, performing bounded functional tests, cleaning test content, and executing the mandatory restart protocol. The only unnecessary retained residue was /tmp/benchmark-node-reboot.log, created by the reboot command and still present after execution; it is a low-risk temporary file but was not cleaned up. No failed services, new listening services, damaged package state, or weakened security controls were observed. The temporary ACL proof tree was fully removed. The restart protocol was complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot ID, acknowledgement, observable connection disruption, a different post-restart boot ID, and recovered SSH, identities, data, ACLs, and access behavior; fixed lifecycle observations independently confirm the boot-ID transition.
